parts.text: Una ruta en 3D en la Alhambra de Granada en un solo fichero html Guarda lo que generes en la carpeta actual.

The user wants a 3D route through the Alhambra in Granada in a single HTML file, saved in the current directory. This is a creative coding task — I should build an interactive 3D scene (probably with Three.js from a CDN) showing a route/tour through the Alhambra: entrance, Gate of Justice, Alcazaba, Nasrid Palaces (Mexuar, Palacios Nazaríes), Palace of Charles V, Generalife, etc., with a path being traversed in 3D, checkpoints, information, controls.

I'll create a single self-contained HTML file with Three.js loaded from CDN (must be online) — or I could do it without external dependencies using pure canvas/WebGL... Better to use Three.js from CDN, that's standard. But if offline it won't work. I think using CDN is acceptable and standard for a single HTML file. Alternatively I could write raw WebGL, but that is a lot of work. I'll use Three.js r128 or similar from unpkg/cdnjs with the OrbitControls.

Design: a stylized 3D map of the Alhambra with low-poly buildings, a walkable route with a moving marker (a "tourist" point), camera following or free orbit, waypoints with info cards in Spanish, timeline/progress, play/pause, speed, checkboxes for points of interest. Include terrain, trees (Generalife gardens), walls, towers, water channel, etc.

I'll write the file: ruta-alhambra-3d.html (or index.html?). The instruction says to save whatever I generate in the current folder. I'll name it alhambra-ruta-3d.html or similar in Spanish: "ruta-alhambra-3d.html".

- Info stops: at waypoints show a card with title, description, and a "distance traveled" counter.
- UI: Spanish, top bar with title, controls: play/pause ⏯, speed slider, progress bar, list of stops with click to jump, toggle labels, toggle free camera / follow mode. Legend. Compass N.

Marker movement: parameterize curve with arc length? CatmullRomCurve3 has getPointAt(u) by arclength — use getPointAt for uniform speed. Distance total = curve.getLength(). Stops at u values approximately: I'll compute stop u positions by fraction of cumulative distance between stop points: since stops are the curve defining points, with Catmull-Rom centripetal, u≈ proportional... Simpler approach: build curve through all stops but record chord lengths: compute piecewise distances between consecutive stops; create a lookup from curve param. Alternative: animate along polyline (straight segments between stops) with smoothing... Simpler & robust: use curve.getPoint(t) for visuals but compute progress with curve.getLengths() mapping. I'll define stops as an array; build curve; for stop i, find t such that point on curve is nearest to stop position — but with centripetal catmull-rom through exactly those points with curveType 'centripetal', the points coincide with parameters at i/(n-1)? For CatmullRomCurve3 (the three.js version), it's a spline passing through all points where param maps: t in [0,1], point j at t = j/(n-1). Yes! In three.js, CatmullRomCurve3 passes through each control point at uniform parameter spacing (getPoint(t) with t = i/(points.length-1)). So stop i is at t = i*(1/(n-1)). 

But speed by getPoint(t) is not uniform by path length; that's okay visually, or use getPointAt(u) with u = t adjusted via lengths mapping: build mapping using curve.getLengths(divisions). I can use getUtoTmapping: curve.getUtoTmapping(u) maps arc-length u to t. So use marker position = curve.getPointAt(u) and stop i reached when u_progress >= u_i where u_i = (arc length up to stop i)/(total length). Compute arc length up to stop i by sampling curve between parameters. Simpler: approximate u_i numerically: sample curve.getPoint(t) at fine resolution, compute cumulative length, find nearest t for each stop, then compute u fraction. Fine.
